thread.title: EUROPE MARKETS: European Stocks End Lower Amid Fresh Italian Jitters; Tech Shares Hit 17-year High

author: morningstar.com
title: EUROPE MARKETS: European Stocks End Lower Amid Fresh Italian Jitters; Tech Shares Hit 17-year High
text:
By Carla Mozee, MarketWatch
RBS shares drop as U.K. government further reduces stake in the lender
Italian stock and bond prices finished lower Tuesday, weighing on the broader European equity bourses, as the country's new prime minister outlined the coalition government's vision for the eurozone's third-largest economy.
However, European tech stocks overall were pushed to a multiyear high, bolstered by gains for their Wall Street counterparts.
How markets performed
The Stoxx Europe 600 Index ended down by 0.3% at 386.89, as financial shares lost the most while tech shares climbed. On Monday, the benchmark rose 0.3% (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-rise-as-ma-cheer-replaces-political-fears-2018-06-04) and marked its best finish in a week.
Pressure came from a slump in Italian stocks. The FTSE MIB index stumbled 1.2% to end at 21,750.15. Italian bond prices also fell, pushing the country's 2-year bond yield up by 28 basis points to 0.99%, according to Tradeweb. Yields rise when bond prices fall.
U.K. blue-chips declined as well, leaving the FTSE 100 down by 0.7% to 7,686.80. That index fell victim to a rise in the , which climbed following a better-than-expected report on British services-sector activity in May.
Germany's DAX 30 index rose 0.1% to 12,787.13, paring an intraday rise of roughly 1%. France's CAC 40 index fell 0.2% to close at 5,494.88. Spain's IBEX 35 fell 0.7% at 9,686.40.
The euro rose to $1.1722 Tuesday following reports that the European Central Bank would use its June 14 policy meeting to discuss an exit from its quantitative-easing program (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/euro-turns-higher-on-report-ecb-to-weigh-qe-exit-plans-2018-06-05). Late Monday, the shared currency bought $1.1699.
See:Why a bet against the dollar makes sense as trade-war fears fester (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/why-a-bet-against-the-dollar-makes-sense-as-trade-war-fears-fester-2018-06-04)
What drove markets
The Stoxx Europe 600 was dragged into the red as losses in Italian stocks accelerated. Investors started to ditch Italian equities as Giuseppe Conte, Italy's new prime minister, outlined "radical change" from the country's new coalition government.
Conte, in his first address to Italy's senate said the government--held between the antiestablishment 5 Star Movement and the League parties--wants to cut the country's heavy debt load by fostering economic growth through welfare spending and cutting taxes. Italy's debt exceeds roughly 130% of the country's gross domestic product.
"We want to reduce [debt] through the growth of our wealth, not with the austerity that has contributed to its rising," Conte said, according to Dow Jones Newswires.
A confidence vote on the new government, which was sworn in on Friday, was to be held in the Senate on Tuesday, while another vote was expected Wednesday in the lower house.
Italian stocks and bonds have been volatile in recent sessions as a previous governing agreement between the 5 Star Movement and the League parties crumbled last week, but a new deal revived the union.
Read:ECB cut back buying of Italian bonds in May, drawing Rome's ire (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ecb-cut-back-buying-of-italian-bonds-in-may-feeding-suspicions-of-meddling-2018-06-04)
Also check out:Not so fast on Italy--expect conflict and trouble within the new coalition (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/not-so-fast-on-italy-expect-conflict-and-trouble-within-the-new-coalition-2018-05-29)
Meanwhile, European tech shares strengthened, sending the Stoxx Europe 600 Technology Index up 1.5% to hit its highest since 2001, FactSet data showed. Semiconductor stocks were among top performers, with ASM International NV (ASMIY) ending up 5.8% and STMicroelectronics NV (STM) finishing up 4.3%.
The moves followed Monday's tech-fueled rally on Wall Street that left the Nasdaq Composite at its first record close since March 12 (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/wall-street-poised-for-higher-open-as-jobs-optimism-outweighs-trade-fears-2018-06-04), buoyed in part by Apple Inc. (AAPL). The iPhone maker's shares hit a new all-time high on Monday, the first day of the company's WWDC developer conference (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/apples-wwdc-no-immediate-catalysts-to-get-to-1-trillion-market-cap-2018-06-04). Apple shares were gaining ground as European trading closed.
What strategists are saying
"With regards to [Italy's ] fiscal expansion in particular, the new government's problem is twofold," said Norbert Aul, a strategist at UBS, wrote in an early Tuesday research note. "[O]n the one hand, Italy has undertaken the obligation to continue consolidating its fiscal position in order to satisfy the requirements of the Stability and Growth Pact and the Fiscal Compact; and, on the other, it also faces market constraints due to the high level of government debt," he said.
"This means that well before the government is in a position to negotiate its fiscal plans with Brussels, there are limits to the fiscal expansion the market may be willing to allow the new government to undertake," Aul wrote.
Stock movers
Italian bank stocks finished lower, with investors concerned about their exposure to Italian government debt. UniCredit SpA (UCG.MI) fell 3.6%, Intesa Sanpaolo SpA (ISP.MI) gave up 3.8% and BPER Banca SpA (BPE.MI) lost 3.4%.
Sticking with banks, Royal Bank of Scotland (RBS.LN)(RBS.LN) shares dropped 5.3% to GBP2.66. That's below the GBP2.71-a-share price at which the U.K. government late Monday sold shares as it unloaded another 7.7% stake in the lender (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/uk-government-sells-77-rbs-stake-for-251-bln-2018-06-05-34852818). British taxpayers paid on average GBP5 per RBS share during a bailout 10 years ago.
Smurfit Kappa Group PLC shares (SK3.DB)slid 6.4%, the biggest decliner on the Stoxx 600, as a Wednesday deadline approached for International Paper Co. (IP)to make a new buyout offer or walk away (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/smurfit-kappa-continues-to-reject-approach-from-ip-2018-05-16), an Irish takeover paneled had ruled in May. Last month, Smurfit rejected an EUR8.9 billion euro ($10.6 billion) takeover approach from IP.
EasyJet PLC (EZJ.LN) fell 2.5% even after a ratings upgrade to hold from sell at Liberum. Meanwhile, Air France-KLM (AF.FR) was dragged down 5%, with Bernstein Research saying "problems are mounting" for the airline, including competition in its core domestic market and a running battle with French unions. The Stoxx Europe 600 Travel & Leisure closed down by 0.7%.
Economic data
The final May readings on eurozone services activity came in at 53.8 from IHS Markit versus April's print of 53.9. The U.K.'s services sector PMI was 54.0, higher than a FactSet consensus estimate at 53.1, and up from April's reading of 52.8.
